audience: Businesses with a defined exit event
objective: Help business owners understand when a short-term facility suits versus a longer-term commitment.

slides.headline: Short-Term vs Long-Term Finance
slides.subheadline: Matching the term to the need.

slides.headline: What's the real difference?
slides.body: Short-term finance typically runs from a few months up to around two years, suited to a defined, time-bound need with a clear exit event. Long-term finance extends over several years, better suited to larger capital investments where repayments are spread across a longer horizon.

slides.headline: Term length should match the need, not the other way around.
slides.body: A mismatch either way can cost more than necessary — subject to lender assessment and approval.

caption:
Taking a long-term facility for a short-term need — or vice versa — is one of the more common structuring mistakes we see.

Short-term finance suits a defined, time-bound situation with a clear exit event. Long-term finance suits larger investments where spreading repayments over years makes more sense than compressing them into months.
